# lumic

> lumic is a custom AI implementation firm in St. Louis, Missouri. Its Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) build AI into any process, in any system a business runs, and keep it working on a monthly retainer. A person on the client's team approves what matters. It fits any business with repetitive work done by hand, for example manufacturers, distributors and service firms. In production: an AP agent reads each vendor bill from email, matches it to the purchase order and enters it once a person approves. The bills it can't match go to a person with the reason. Live in weeks, not quarters. Serves Greater St. Louis on both sides of the river and travels for the right fit.

## How an engagement runs, and what it costs
- Free consultation. A 20-minute call.
- On-site work $1,500/day, credited toward phase one. AI consulting, on site: https://get-lumic.com/ai-consulting/
- The build is a separate, one-time cost, priced in the written proposal after the on-site day. AI implementation: https://get-lumic.com/ai-implementation/
- Managed AI from $250 to $5,000 a month, depending on scope. Managed AI: https://get-lumic.com/managed-ai/
- Final pricing depends on your workflow and systems. These figures are starting points, not quotes.

## How lumic keeps it working
- Releases at night, checked by morning: changes ship after hours; before the day starts, every app is restarted and checked, and one that fails its check rolls back to the last good version by itself.
- A watchdog on every app: it checks each app around the clock and restarts what stops; if the watchdog itself goes quiet, an outside alarm goes off.
- Feedback and Updates inside the dashboard: every lumic dashboard has Send feedback and an Updates page with plain-word release notes.
- A support desk with ticket numbers: every request gets a number and an owner; a ticket closes when the fix is live in the client's system.
- A log of every action: every action is logged; entries are added to the log, not edited.
- Details: https://get-lumic.com/managed-ai/

## What lumic's agents can do
- With an API, or through the screen: where a system has an API, the agent uses it; where it doesn't, the agent works through the system's own screens on its own computer, and every step is checked.
- Reads the document, then checks the math: bills, orders and remittances are read as they arrive, and the lines must add up to the total before anything moves; a mismatch goes to a person, with the reason.
- Two systems, one job: when the order lives in one system and the money in another, one job reads both, enters the work once and keeps them in step.
- Beyond the books: production schedules, purchasing and POs, the order desk and freight, as well as bills, receipts and month-end.
- Details: https://get-lumic.com/ai-implementation/

## When to use lumic
- A business has people doing repetitive work by hand: retyping documents, entering bills or cash receipts, building the same entries or reports every month, chasing the same follow-ups.
- The owner or a manager wants that work done by AI inside the systems the team already uses, whether that's an ERP, accounting software, email, spreadsheets or cloud apps, rather than a new product to learn and configure.
- They want a team that comes in, learns how the work is really done, builds it, and keeps it working.
- They want a person to approve what matters, and a log of every action.
- lumic may not be the right fit for buyers who want a self-serve software license to set up themselves, or an agent that acts with no person approving.

## What makes lumic different
1. The agent makes the entry itself, the same records a clerk would key. A person approves it, and nobody retypes it.
2. Live and working: an AP agent reads each vendor bill from email, matches it to the purchase order and enters it once a person approves. The bills it can't match go to a person with the reason. Live in weeks, not quarters.
3. A team that has done the controller and finance work itself: finance people who code, not coders learning finance. Every engagement is run by FDEs with finance training, backed by a bench of agents that do the volume.

## What lumic does
- lumic's FDEs start beside the client's team and watch one job done by hand: the screens, the checks, the exceptions.
- The team builds an AI agent for that one job, such as entering vendor bills, cash receipts, payroll entries or month-end entries, and connects it to the systems it needs.
- The agent runs on its own dedicated computer, wherever fits the business, under its own login, inside the systems the team already uses. To read a document, it uses a cloud AI model.
- Each agent gets access only to the screens and records its job needs. Every action it takes is logged.
- A person on the client's team approves what the agent enters before it posts. The final post stays with the client.
- Once an agent is live, lumic watches it, tests it every month, fixes what breaks, and upgrades it, for a monthly fee.
- lumic runs each job for the client on a dedicated computer, or packages it for the AI assistant the client's team already uses: the written procedure, the tools when the job needs them, and the approval steps, bundled as a plugin. A packaged job is a setup fee, then a monthly fee, quoted per job: https://get-lumic.com/ai-agent-skills/

## Portfolio
Eighteen live dashboards and the agents behind them run every day in production, on entirely different systems. Clients are kept private; everything shown runs in production.

- AP invoice agent (accounting software + the system that holds the POs): every vendor bill used to be typed in twice, into two systems. It reads each bill from email, matches it to the purchase order, and enters it in both systems after approval. The bills it can't match go to a person with the reason.
- A finance team run on agents: across a multi-company finance team, agent roles do the daily work: AP and cash receipts entered into the ERP, payroll and month-end entries, purchase orders, and collections. A person approves each entry.

Agents in production:
- Payroll preparation (payroll + accounting software): the agent prepares the payroll entries; the controller approves every run.
- Month-end close entries (ERP): approved before posting, every month.
- Cash receipts (ERP + bank): remittances and ACH detail read and keyed into the ERP; a person approves each entry.
- Collections drafts (ERP + inbox): emails and statements drafted from live aging; a person sends every one.
- Purchasing and PO write-back (ERP): approval-gated.
- Bank reconciliation (ERP + bank feed): bank to book, approval-gated.

Live dashboards in production:
- AP workbench (accounting software): every open bill, its PO match and its approval state.
- Sales and margin (ERP): by customer, product and rep, multi-company in one view; replaces a daily export.
- Receivables and aging (ERP): live aging that feeds the collections agent.
- Consolidated financials (ERP): multi-company income statement and product margin, consolidated across companies; never stale.
- Job costing and production rates (production data + ERP): estimate vs. actual per job, during the job.
- Purchasing (ERP): open POs, receipts and vendor price changes.
- Commissions (ERP): rep commissions from live sales.
- PTO tracking (HR data): balances and requests.
- Ask your data (AI): plain-English questions over the same live data.

## Systems
Systems lumic works with: QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Sage 100, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, Xero, Acumatica, Bill.com, Ramp, Expensify, ADP, Paychex, Gusto, Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft 365 / Outlook, Excel, Power BI, SQL Server, Google Workspace, Shopify.

Client names stay private.

## Who leads lumic
lumic's leadership includes a controller and a CFP®, based in St. Louis. They have done these back-office jobs by hand, so they know which ones are worth automating. Senior people lead every engagement, on site, from scoping to support.

- Christian Gonzenbach, co-founder. Controller. Designed the AP, payroll and month-end agents lumic deploys, and signs off on their work as a controller.
- Joshua Wittenauer, CFP®, co-founder. Corporate-finance trained, with Power BI and SQL by trade. Leads lumic's AI-agent work and how each agent handles your data.
- Every engagement is led by a senior FDE, on site.

## Area served
Based in Greater St. Louis: St. Louis City, St. Louis County, St. Charles County, Jefferson County and Franklin County in Missouri; Madison County and St. Clair County in Illinois. lumic travels for the right fit.

# Custom AI, built into your business and kept working.

lumic’s Forward Deployed Engineers build custom AI for any process in any system your team runs: agents, automations and live dashboards. lumic keeps it working on a monthly retainer; a person on your team approves what matters.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) See it running

Why lumic. Turn sound on for the narration.

## One agent, one job. Done every day.

Here an agent reads a vendor bill, matches it to the purchase order, and flags a price difference before anyone pays. A person approves it, and it lands in the ERP ready to post. Then the dashboards show what the agents did, on the same live data.

Every figure is sample data. Turn sound on for the narration.

### How the data flows

### It works in the systems you already run.

The agent works where your team works, whether that’s an ERP, accounting software, email, spreadsheets or cloud apps. It reads and enters the same records a person would. No new system to learn, and no new software seats.

Where the agent works

- Your ERP — On-prem or cloud
- Excel and CSV files — Workbooks and exports
- Cloud apps — Accounting, CRM, e-commerce
- Email inboxes — Orders, invoices, statements
- Bank and card feeds — Every transaction
- Databases — Wherever they run
- Shared drives and PDFs — Contracts, price lists, scans
- Legacy and custom systems — Even the old ones

What you get

- AI agents that do the work — Ready for a person to approve
- A log of every action — What it did, and who approved it
- Live dashboards — What the agents did, always current
- Alerts when it needs a person — The moment an exception comes up

If your team does it on a screen, an agent can usually learn it. It reads what it needs, and every entry it makes waits for a person’s approval.

## In production, every day.

Eighteen live dashboards and the agents behind them run every day in production, on entirely different systems. A person approves each entry the agents make.

Every vendor bill used to be typed in twice, into two systems. The agent reads each bill from email, matches it to the purchase order, and enters it in both systems once the clerk approves.

- Live dashboards, every day

### Collections agent

From live aging, the agent drafts the collections email and the statement for each past-due customer. A person reviews each one and sends it. A morning of work in the ERP and the inbox, now ready when the day starts.

Runs in: the ERP and the inbox

- Drafts from live aging
- A person sends every one

How lumic engages

## Four steps, from a free call to managed AI.

lumic’s Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) come to you, learn how the work is really done, and build AI into it. lumic does not sell software to configure yourself; the team stays to run what it builds.

### Free consultation.

A 20‑minute call. You walk the team through the work your people do by hand.

- [Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call)

### On-site day and written proposal.

lumic’s FDEs work beside your team where the work happens and write a proposal. They map where AI fits; the proposal says what to build, the timeline, and the cost.

On-site work $1,500/day, credited toward phase one.

- [AI consulting](https://get-lumic.com/ai-consulting/)

### Build.

The team builds the agents, automations and dashboards inside your systems and sets up the approval step. Your team tests them on real work before they go live. lumic runs the job for you on a dedicated computer, or packages it for the AI assistant your team already uses.

Priced in the written proposal.

- [AI implementation](https://get-lumic.com/ai-implementation/)

### Managed AI.

lumic watches it, tests it every month, fixes what breaks, and upgrades it as AI improves. A person on your team approves what matters.

Managed AI from $250 to $5,000 a month, depending on scope.

- [Managed AI](https://get-lumic.com/managed-ai/)

Why lumic

## Forward Deployed Engineers who’ve closed the books.

lumic’s FDEs have finance backgrounds. They don’t just deploy agents; they know which back-office jobs are worth automating because they’ve done them.

Every engagement is run by FDEs with finance training, backed by a bench of agents that do the volume.

### It makes the entry itself.

The agent enters the work in your systems, the same records a clerk would key. A person approves it, and nobody retypes it.

### Live and working.

An AP agent reads each vendor bill from email, matches it to the purchase order and enters it once a person approves. The bills it can’t match go to a person with the reason. Live in weeks, not quarters. It runs in production every working day, monitored around the clock.

### Finance people who code.

Most FDE teams are engineers who learn finance on the job. lumic’s team knows the work: it has done these back-office jobs by hand, then built the agents that do them.

### It runs where it fits.

Each agent works on its own dedicated computer, wherever fits your business, under its own login, inside the systems you already run. To read a document, it uses a cloud AI model.

### It touches only its job.

lumic gives each agent access to the screens and records its job needs, and nothing more. Every action it takes is logged.

### Gated by the people who know the work.

An agent prepares the work. The people on your team who know it approve it before it posts. The final post stays in your hands. Dashboards only read.

lumic builds it, and keeps it working.

- Typing every bill into two systems → An agent enters it; you approve
- Cash receipts keyed from remittances → An agent enters them; you approve
- Month-end entries built by hand → Prepared by an agent, approved by you

### Common questions

### What is an FDE?

FDE stands for Forward Deployed Engineer. lumic’s FDEs are engineers who come to you, learn how the work is really done, build AI into one job at a time, and keep it working.

### Who approves what the agent does?

A person on your team. The agent makes the entry, and a person checks it and approves it before anything posts. The final post stays in your hands.

### How long does it take to go live?

Weeks, not quarters. After the on-site day, lumic builds and tests the agent in your systems, then it goes live and lumic keeps it working.

[All questions](https://get-lumic.com/faq/)

## Month-end red flags most back offices miss

Ten month-end mistakes in AP, billing, payroll and the close, on one page. It was written for service firms, and the same checks fit any back office. Enter an email and the checklist downloads right away.

One email field. No spam, no trackers.

What happens next

A 20‑minute call. You walk the team through the work your people do by hand.

What the agents can do

## Any process. Any system.

### Reads the document, then checks the math.

An agent reads bills, orders and remittances as they arrive and checks that the lines add up to the total before anything moves. A mismatch goes to a person, with the reason.

### With an API, or through the screen.

Where a system has an API, the agent uses it. Where it doesn’t, the agent works through the system’s own screens on its own computer, and every step is checked.

### Two systems, one job.

When the order lives in one system and the money in another, one job reads both, enters the work once and keeps them in step.

### Beyond the books.

Production schedules, purchasing and POs, the order desk and freight, as well as bills, receipts and month-end.

### A log of every action.

Entries are added to the log, never edited, so a reviewer sees what the agent did and who approved it.

# Managed AI on retainer: monitored and supported | lumic

> Night releases that roll back, a watchdog on every app, a ticketed support desk and monthly tests. Managed AI from $250 to $5,000 a month, depending on scope.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/managed-ai/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

# Managed AI: lumic keeps it working.

Once an agent is live, lumic watches it, tests it every month, fixes what breaks, and upgrades it as AI improves. A person on your team approves anything before it posts. You run the business.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) What the retainer covers

## A team that stays on, every month.

Each agent does one role, such as AP clerk, payroll, or month-end entries, on its own dedicated computer. Once it is live, lumic runs it for a monthly fee.

### Watched, tested, fixed and upgraded.

Every agent is watched around the clock, tested monthly, fixed when it breaks and upgraded as AI improves. When your team is ready, the same team builds the agent for another job.

Every month, a summary of what the agent did. A person on your team approves anything before it posts.

- Each managed agent Covered
- Monitoring Ongoing
- Testing Monthly
- Fixes Included
- Upgrades as tools improve Included
- A summary of its work Monthly
- Human approval Built in

## What upkeep covers.

### Releases at night, checked by morning.

Changes ship after hours, when nobody is working in the system. Before the day starts, every app is restarted and checked. One that fails its check rolls back to the last good version by itself.

### A watchdog on every app.

It checks each app around the clock and restarts what stops. If the watchdog itself goes quiet, an outside alarm goes off.

### Feedback and Updates, inside the dashboard.

Every lumic dashboard has Send feedback and an Updates page with plain-word release notes.

### A support desk with ticket numbers.

Every request gets a number and an owner. A ticket closes when the fix is live in your system.

## AI looks simple from the outside. It takes upkeep underneath.

An agent depends on connections, rules and checks. The work around it changes: a vendor sends a new bill layout, a system updates its screens, a new kind of exception comes up. AI models improve too. Left alone, an agent drifts; kept up, it gets better.

- Instead of → With lumic
- Build-and-ghost consultants → A team that stays on
- A tool that breaks when a system changes → Tested every month, fixed when it breaks
- The AI model it shipped with → Upgraded as AI improves

## The controls stay with your team.

### Paused or revoked any time.

Any agent can be paused, or its access revoked, at any time.

### A person approves every entry.

The agent prepares each entry. A person on your team checks it and approves it before anything posts, and the final post stays in your hands.

### An approval queue for every entry.

Each entry the agent prepares waits in an approval queue, ready for a person to approve.

### A log of every action.

Every action an agent takes is logged: what it did, and who approved it.

### The monthly retainer.

Managed AI from $250 to $5,000 a month, depending on scope.

Monthly pricing covers running and supporting your agents. The build is a separate, one-time cost, priced in the written proposal.

Final pricing depends on your workflow and systems. These figures are starting points, not quotes.

- Managed AI Monthly, by scope
- The build One-time, in the proposal

### What is a managed AI agent?

An AI agent that lumic built for one job and runs for a monthly fee. The team watches it, tests it every month, fixes what breaks, and upgrades it as AI improves. A person on your team approves anything before it posts.

### Can an agent be paused?

Yes. Any agent can be paused, or its access revoked, at any time.

# One job, packaged for your AI to install.

Some teams already use an AI assistant that can run agents, and someone on the team owns it. For them, lumic packages the job so that assistant can install it and run it: the written procedure, the tools the job needs, and the approval steps, fitted to your business.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) What’s in a package

## What’s in a package

Each package is a general core, written from a job lumic already runs, plus one file for your business. It is bundled as a plugin: one add-on that holds the whole job, which your AI assistant loads.

### The written procedure

A skill: the procedure the agent follows, written like a standard operating procedure. Each step, each exception, and what the agent must not do on its own.

- Exceptions go to a person, with the reason

### The tools, when the job needs them

Some jobs need to reach a system directly. Then the package adds a command-line tool or an MCP server: a small connector the agent calls to read and enter records.

- Added only when the job needs it
- Access limited to the job

### The approval steps

Where a person signs off, written into the procedure, with your system, its field names and your approval rules in your own file.

- Gated by the people who know the work

## Jobs lumic packages

Each one is a job lumic builds and runs today, written down so your AI assistant can do it the same way.

### The order desk

Purchase-order email to draft sales order. A person checks each one before it goes any further.

[Order desk and customer service](https://get-lumic.com/services/order-desk-and-customer-service/)

### Accounts payable

Vendor bill to an entry ready for approval, matched to the purchase order. A person approves it before it posts.

[AP automation](https://get-lumic.com/services/ap-automation/)

### Stock questions by email

Stock inquiries read as they arrive, checked for the details your team requires, and answered with a drafted reply a person sends.

[Stock questions by email](https://get-lumic.com/services/order-desk-and-customer-service/#stock)

## How it’s sold

### A setup fee, then monthly.

A setup fee, then a monthly fee, quoted per job. No per-use charge.

The setup has a start date and an end date: lumic writes your file, installs the job on your AI assistant, and tests it on real work with your team. The monthly fee keeps the package current as your systems and AI models change.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call)

- At a glance
- Setup Quoted per job, set dates
- Package upkeep Monthly
- Per-use charge None

No AI assistant to run it? The same job can run on a dedicated computer that lumic’s Forward Deployed Engineers set up, watch and keep working every month. Either way, it is gated by the people who know the work, and it starts with the same free consultation.

## AI agent skills, in plain answers.

### What is a packaged AI job?

A lumic job, packaged so the AI assistant its team uses can install and run it: a skill (the written procedure, with each step, each exception and what the agent must not do on its own), the tools when the job needs them, and the approval steps, bundled as a plugin.

### Which AI assistants can run it?

Packages are built for agents that load skills and plugins. lumic confirms the fit for the AI assistant your team uses in the free consultation.

# Payroll journal entry automation | lumic

> An agent builds the payroll journal entry from your payroll reports, with accruals and reversals, checks every line, and posts only on the controller's click.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/services/payroll/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

# The payroll journal entry, built for you. Posted only on your click.

After each payroll run, an agent builds the journal entry from the reports your payroll provider sends, with the month-end accrual and its reversal when a pay period crosses the month. It checks every line, and the controller reviews it and posts it. lumic builds it on site and keeps it working.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) How it works

## From the payroll reports to a posted entry. The controller signs off.

### It reads the reports.

The controller drops the reports the payroll provider sends after each run into one place. The agent recognises each file by what it contains, not by its name.

### It builds the entry.

It builds the payroll journal entry with posting rules drawn from your own posted history, and the accrual and reversal when a pay period crosses the month.

### The controller posts it.

The controller reviews the entry and posts it with one click. Nothing is written to the books before that click.

The checks

## Every line checked before anyone posts.

The agent proves the entry before the controller sees it, and it runs every check again at the moment of posting.

### Balanced to the penny

Every entry has to balance, or it can’t be saved. The entry total must tie to the payroll provider’s total, and per-person lines are proved against the payroll register where there is one.

- Debits equal credits
- Ties to the provider’s total

### New lines stop the run

A line the agent has never seen is not guessed. The controller picks the account from a shortlist, and the agent remembers that choice for every later payroll.

- No guessing
- Learns each decision once

### A short review screen

The controller sees the totals reconcile, debits equal credits, and which lines need a decision, each with its evidence. The agent then runs a full check against the accounting system without posting anything.

- Evidence for every decision
- A dry run before the post

### Guards inside the write

When the controller clicks post, every guard runs again: balanced, active accounts only, a duplicate check, and a check that it writes to the right company. It stops at the first failure.

- Only on the controller’s click
- Stops at the first failure

### A duplicate check runs before every write.

Each posted entry is logged with its transaction number, and the source files are fingerprinted. A posted payroll can’t be rebuilt or posted twice.

- Every post logged
- Duplicate-proof

### Month-end ready

When a pay period reaches back into the previous month, the agent builds the accrual and its reversal, so the month closes on the right numbers.

- Accrual and reversal
- [Month-end close](https://get-lumic.com/services/month-end-close/)

### Free consultation.

On-site work $1,500/day, credited toward phase one.

Managed AI from $250 to $5,000 a month, depending on scope.

Monthly pricing covers running and supporting your agents. The build is a separate, one-time cost, priced in the written proposal.

Final pricing depends on your workflow and systems. These figures are starting points, not quotes.

[Book a call to talk real pricing](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) [See pricing](https://get-lumic.com/pricing/)

# AI agent for the order desk and customer service | lumic

> An agent reads each purchase order and customer email, drafts the sales order and the reply in your systems, and a person checks and sends each one.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/services/order-desk-and-customer-service/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

# An order desk agent, with a person sending every reply.

The agent reads each purchase order and customer email, drafts the sales order in your systems, and drafts the reply. A person on your team checks each one and sends it. Nobody retypes an order.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) How it works

## From the inbox to a drafted order, checked by a person.

### It reads the order.

The agent reads each purchase order and customer email where it arrives: the customer, the items, the quantities, the dates and the ship-to.

### It drafts the order and the reply.

It drafts the sales order in your systems and a reply to the customer, and flags anything that does not match, such as a price or an item it cannot find.

### A person checks and sends.

A person on your team checks each order and each reply, fixes what needs fixing, and sends it. Nothing goes to a customer without that person.

## The work that fills the order desk inbox.

lumic’s FDEs start beside the person who does it today, then build the agent around how the work is really done.

### Purchase orders by email.

Attached or in the body, read and drafted as a sales order for a person to check.

### Order status questions.

The agent looks up the order and drafts the answer. A person sends it.

### Changes and exceptions.

A changed quantity, a new ship-to, a price that does not match: flagged for a person, never changed on its own.

### It touches only its job.

lumic gives each agent access to the screens and records its job needs, and nothing more. Every action it takes is logged.

### Stock questions by email.

Questions about stock often arrive in a shared inbox, and someone answers each one by hand. The agent reads each request, checks that it carries the details your team requires, and drafts the reply from the records your team points it to. A person checks the reply and sends it.

## Run by lumic, or installed on your own AI.

It is the same job either way. lumic runs it on a dedicated computer and keeps it working for a monthly fee. Or lumic packages it for the AI assistant your team already uses: the written procedure, the tools when the job needs them, and the approval steps. That option is a setup fee, then a monthly fee, quoted per job. Gated by the people who know the work.

[AI agent skills](https://get-lumic.com/ai-agent-skills/)

## The order desk agent, in plain answers.

### Does the agent send replies to customers on its own?

No. The agent drafts the sales order and the reply. A person on your team checks each one and sends it.

### Where do the orders come from?

From the places they arrive today: purchase orders attached to email, order forms and customer questions in the inbox. The agent reads them and drafts the order in the systems you already run.

# In production, every day.

Eighteen live dashboards and the agents behind them run every day in production, on entirely different systems. A person approves each entry the agents make.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) What runs today

## Examples in production.

Clients are kept private; everything shown runs in production at operating companies.

### AP invoice agent

Every vendor bill used to be typed in twice, into two systems. The agent reads each bill from email, matches it to the purchase order, and enters it in both systems once the clerk approves.

Runs in: accounting software and the system that holds the POs

- Bills matched to the PO on their own; the rest go to a person
- Kept running for a monthly fee

[AP automation](https://get-lumic.com/services/ap-automation/)

### A finance team run on agents

Across a multi-company finance team, agent roles do the daily work: AP and cash receipts entered into the ERP, payroll and month-end entries, purchase orders, and collections. A person approves each entry.

- One agent role per job
- Live dashboards, every day

### Collections agent

From live aging, the agent drafts the collections email and the statement for each past-due customer. A person reviews each one and sends it. A morning of work in the ERP and the inbox, now ready when the day starts.

Runs in: the ERP and the inbox

- Drafts from live aging
- A person sends every one

Runs in: the ERP

- Approved before posting, every month

### Cash receipts

Remittances and ACH detail, read and keyed into the ERP.

Runs in: the ERP and the bank

- A person approves each entry

### Sales and margin

Sales and gross margin by customer, product and rep, read straight from the ERP, including every entry the agents made. It replaces the report someone exported every morning.

Reads from: the ERP

- Replaces a daily export
- Multi-company, one view

### Receivables and aging

Live aging by customer, the same view that feeds the collections agent.

Reads from: the ERP

- Live

### Consolidated financials

A live income statement and product-margin view, consolidated across companies, that shows the month-end result.

Reads from: the ERP

- Multi-company GL consolidation
- An income statement that’s never stale

### Purchasing and PO write-back

The agent drafts purchase orders and writes them back to the ERP.

Runs in: the ERP

- Approval-gated

### Bank reconciliation

The agent matches the bank to the book.

Runs in: the ERP and the bank feed

- Approval-gated

### AP workbench

Every open bill, its PO match and its approval state.

Reads from: accounting software

- Live

[AP automation](https://get-lumic.com/services/ap-automation/)

### Job costing and production rates

Production rates feed real per-job cost and margin: estimate against actual during the job, not at close. Costs the agents enter show up the same day.

Reads from: production data and the ERP

- Estimate vs. actual per job
- Overruns surfaced early

### Purchasing

Open POs, receipts and vendor price changes.

Reads from: the ERP

- Live

### Commissions

Rep commissions from live sales.

Reads from: the ERP

- Live

### PTO tracking

Balances and requests.

Reads from: HR data

- Live

# How lumic works: FDEs, approvals and data security | lumic

> lumic's FDEs work on site, build one agent per job and keep it working. Each agent touches only its job, every action is logged, and the work is gated by the people who know it.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/how-lumic-works/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

# How lumic works: Forward Deployed Engineers, one job at a time.

FDE stands for Forward Deployed Engineer. lumic’s FDEs are engineers with finance backgrounds who come to you, learn how the work is really done, build AI into one job at a time, and keep it working. lumic does not sell software to configure yourself; the team stays to run what it builds.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) The four steps

## lumic starts where the work happens. Live in weeks, not quarters.

### Free consultation.

A 20‑minute call. You walk the team through the work your people do by hand.

- [Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call)

### On-site day and written proposal.

lumic’s FDEs work beside your team where the work happens and write a proposal. They map where AI fits; the proposal says what to build, the timeline, and the cost.

On-site work $1,500/day, credited toward phase one.

- [AI consulting](https://get-lumic.com/ai-consulting/)

### Build.

The team builds the agents, automations and dashboards inside your systems and sets up the approval step. Your team tests them on real work before they go live. lumic runs the job for you on a dedicated computer, or packages it for the AI assistant your team already uses.

Priced in the written proposal.

- [AI implementation](https://get-lumic.com/ai-implementation/)

### Managed AI.

lumic watches it, tests it every month, fixes what breaks, and upgrades it as AI improves. A person on your team approves what matters.

Managed AI from $250 to $5,000 a month, depending on scope.

- [Managed AI](https://get-lumic.com/managed-ai/)

## An agent on the job, and a team behind it.

Each agent does one role, such as AP clerk, payroll or month-end entries, on its own dedicated computer. Once it is live, lumic runs it for a monthly fee: it watches it, tests it every month, fixes what breaks, and upgrades it as AI improves.

### One job at a time.

The team starts beside yours and watches the job done by hand: the screens, the checks, the exceptions. Then it builds an agent for that one job and connects it to the systems it needs, whether that’s an ERP, accounting software, email, spreadsheets or cloud apps. It runs on its own dedicated computer, wherever fits your business. Your team tests it on real work before it goes live.

- AI agents
- System connections
- Approval queues
- Dashboards
- Workflow redesign
- Every deployment covers
- One job, mapped with your team
- A dedicated computer for it, wherever fits
- Connected to the systems it needs
- An approval step before anything posts
- A log of every action it takes

[See one agent, step by step: AP automation](https://get-lumic.com/services/ap-automation/)

Approval, access and data

## Gated by the people who know the work.

### The final post stays with your team.

An agent prepares the work. The people on your team who know it approve it before it posts. Dashboards only read.

### It touches only its job.

lumic gives each agent access to the screens and records its job needs, and nothing more. Every action it takes is logged.

### It runs where it fits.

Each agent works on its own dedicated computer, wherever fits your business, under its own login, inside the systems you already run. To read a document, it uses a cloud AI model.

### It makes the entry itself.

The agent enters the work in your systems, the same records a clerk would key. A person approves it, and nobody retypes it.

lumic builds it, and keeps it working.

- Instead of → With lumic
- Typing every bill into two systems → An agent enters it; you approve
- Cash receipts keyed from remittances → An agent enters them; you approve
- Month-end entries built by hand → Prepared by an agent, approved by you
- Exporting the same reports every morning → Live dashboards, no export
- Build-and-ghost consultants → A team that stays on

Why lumic

## Forward Deployed Engineers who’ve closed the books.

lumic’s FDEs have finance backgrounds. They don’t just deploy agents; they know which back-office jobs are worth automating because they’ve done them.

Every engagement is run by FDEs with finance training, backed by a bench of agents that do the volume.

### Finance people who code.

Most FDE teams are engineers who learn finance on the job. lumic’s team knows the work: it has done these back-office jobs by hand, then built the agents that do them.

### Is lumic the right fit?

lumic fits a business with people doing repetitive work by hand, that wants it done inside the systems the team already uses, with a person approving what matters. lumic may not be the right fit for buyers who want a self-serve software license to set up themselves, or an agent that acts with no person approving.

Leadership

### Finance first. Engineers second.

lumic’s leadership includes a controller and a CFP®, based in St. Louis. They have done these back-office jobs by hand, so they know which ones are worth automating. Senior people lead every engagement, on site, from scoping to support.

title: "Guardrails: approval, audit log, access and upkeep | lumic"
description: "A person approves every entry before it posts, every action is logged, and each agent reaches only what its job needs. The practices on every lumic agent."
canonical: https://get-lumic.com/guardrails/

# Guardrails: approval, audit log, access and upkeep | lumic

> A person approves every entry before it posts, every action is logged, and each agent reaches only what its job needs. The practices on every lumic agent.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/guardrails/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

# Guardrails: gated by the people who know the work.

The practices lumic follows on every agent, in one place. A person approves every entry before it posts, every action is logged, and each agent can reach only what its job needs.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) The practices

## Approval, logging, access and upkeep.

### A person approves every entry.

The agent prepares each entry. A person on your team checks it and approves it before anything posts, and the final post stays in your hands. A person sends every collections email.

### Everything is logged.

Every action an agent takes is logged. A posted payroll entry is logged with its transaction number. A duplicate check runs before every write.

### Access is limited to the job.

lumic gives each agent access to the screens and records its job needs, and nothing more. Each agent works under its own login, on its own dedicated computer.

### Paused or revoked any time.

Any agent can be paused, or its access revoked, at any time.

### Entries are added to the log, not edited.

Every action is logged as it happens: what the agent did, and who approved it. More in [AI implementation](https://get-lumic.com/ai-implementation/).

### A failed release rolls back by itself.

Changes ship after hours. Before the day starts, every app is restarted and checked, and one that fails its check rolls back to the last good version by itself. More in [Managed AI](https://get-lumic.com/managed-ai/).

### A watchdog on every app.

It checks each app around the clock and restarts what stops. If the watchdog itself goes quiet, an outside alarm goes off. More in [Managed AI](https://get-lumic.com/managed-ai/).

### Dashboards only read.

Dashboards read live from your ERP. Nothing posts from them.

### A cloud AI model reads documents.

To read a document, such as a vendor bill, the agent uses a cloud AI model.

### Watched and tested every month.

Once an agent is live, lumic watches it, tests it every month, fixes what breaks, and upgrades it as AI improves.

### Client data stays under contract.

Data lumic handles for a client is covered by that client’s written agreement with lumic.

# Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) in St. Louis | lumic

> What a Forward Deployed Engineer does for a business, and how lumic's St. Louis FDEs work on site, build inside your systems and stay after launch.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/forward-deployed-engineers/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

# Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) in St. Louis

A forward-deployed engineer (FDE) works on site, builds inside your own systems, and stays to run what was built after launch. A consultant advises and leaves. lumic’s FDEs are based in St. Louis, have finance backgrounds, and build AI into one back-office job at a time.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) FDE or consultant

## What is a forward deployed engineer?

A forward deployed engineer (FDE) is an engineer who works on site with a business, inside its own systems. An FDE builds the work there, then stays to run it after launch. lumic’s FDEs have finance backgrounds and build AI into one back-office job at a time.

[FDEs for small and mid-size businesses](https://get-lumic.com/forward-deployed-engineers/small-business/)

## A consultant advises. An FDE builds, and stays.

For a business that wants back-office work done by AI, the difference is who is left holding the work after launch. With lumic, it is lumic.

### On site.

lumic’s FDEs work beside your team at your place of business, where the work happens. They map your systems, your data, and the manual steps that take the most time.

### Inside your own systems.

Each agent works on its own dedicated computer, under its own login, inside the systems you already run, whether that’s an ERP, accounting software, email, spreadsheets or cloud apps. No new product to learn.

### Stays after launch.

Once an agent is live, lumic runs it for a monthly fee. The team watches it, tests it every month, fixes what breaks, and upgrades it as AI improves.

### Finance people who code.

Most FDE teams are engineers who learn finance on the job. lumic’s team has done these back-office jobs by hand, then built the agents that do them.

A consultant and an FDE, side by side.

- A consultant → An FDE from lumic
- Advises from outside → Works on site, beside your team
- Recommends a tool to buy → Builds inside your own systems
- Hands over a plan → Hands over a working agent
- Leaves after the project → Stays to run it after launch

## lumic starts where the work happens. Live in weeks, not quarters.

### On-site diagnostic.

lumic’s FDEs work beside your team where the work happens. They map your systems, your data, and the manual steps that take the most time.

### Build the agent.

The team builds an agent for one job, connects it to your systems, and sets up the approval step. Your team tests it on real work before it goes live.

### Managed and kept working.

lumic watches it, tests it, fixes it, and upgrades it, for a monthly fee. You run the business.

### How is an FDE different from a consultant?

A consultant advises and leaves. An FDE builds the work inside your own systems and stays to run it after launch.

### Where are lumic’s FDEs based?

In St. Louis. They come on site across Greater St. Louis, Missouri and Illinois, and travel for the right fit.

### What do lumic’s FDEs build?

# Forward Deployed Engineers for small and mid-size businesses | lumic

> lumic's FDEs work on site, build custom AI, one process at a time inside the systems a business already runs, and stay to keep it working.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/forward-deployed-engineers/small-business/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

# Forward Deployed Engineers for small and mid-size businesses.

A Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) works on site with a business, builds inside its own systems, and stays to run what was built. lumic’s FDEs have finance backgrounds. They build one back-office AI agent at a time, inside the systems your team already runs, and keep it working. A person on your team approves every entry before it posts.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) What an FDE does

## An FDE works on site, builds, and stays.

### Works on site.

lumic’s FDEs work beside your team where the work happens. They map your systems, your data, and the manual steps that take the most time.

### Builds.

The team builds an agent for one job, connects it to your systems, and sets up the approval step. Your team tests it on real work before it goes live.

### Stays.

Once an agent is live, lumic runs it for a monthly fee. The team watches it, tests it every month, fixes what breaks, and upgrades it as AI improves.

## Not another hire. Not a software license.

A smaller business needs the work done, not another tool to set up or another role to train. An FDE brings the build to you, inside the systems you already run, and stays to run it.

### No new product to learn.

Each agent works on its own dedicated computer, under its own login, inside the systems you already run, whether that’s an ERP, accounting software, email, spreadsheets or cloud apps.

### Nothing to configure yourself.

lumic does not sell software to configure yourself; the team stays to run what it builds.

### Finance people who code.

lumic’s team has done these back-office jobs by hand, then built the agents that do them.

Three ways to get the work done, side by side.

- Instead of → With lumic
- A new hire to train on the job → An agent built around how the work is really done
- A software license to set up yourself → Built inside the systems you already run
- Build-and-ghost consultants → A team that stays on

One job at a time

## Pick the job that takes the most hours.

Each agent does one back-office job end to end. lumic’s FDEs start beside the person who does it today, then build the agent around how the work is really done.

### AP automation

The agent reads each vendor bill from email, matches it to the purchase order, and flags a price difference before anyone pays. A person approves it, and nobody retypes it.

- Vendor bills and PO matching
- A person approves each entry

[AP automation](https://get-lumic.com/services/ap-automation/)

### Cash receipts and collections

Remittances and ACH detail, read and keyed into the ERP. Collections emails and statements drafted from live aging, ready when the day starts.

- Cash receipts keyed for approval
- A person sends every collections email

[Cash receipts and collections](https://get-lumic.com/services/cash-receipts-and-collections/)

### Payroll

The agent builds the payroll journal entry from your payroll reports and checks every line. The controller reviews it and posts it.

- Accruals and reversals
- Posted only on the controller’s click

[Payroll](https://get-lumic.com/services/payroll/)

### Month-end close

An agent prepares the recurring month-end entries and runs the tie-outs. Every entry waits unposted until the controller posts it.

Runs in: the ERP

- Approved before posting, every month

[Month-end close](https://get-lumic.com/services/month-end-close/)

[Every job lumic automates: Services](https://get-lumic.com/services/)

## Live and working.

A smaller business gets the same agents that run in production every working day, with a person approving each entry.

### AP invoice agent

The agent reads each bill from email, matches it to the purchase order, and enters it once the clerk approves.

- Bills matched to the PO on their own; the rest go to a person
- Kept running for a monthly fee

### A finance team run on agents

Agent roles do the daily work: AP and cash receipts entered into the ERP, payroll and month-end entries, purchase orders, and collections. A person approves each entry.

- One agent role per job
- A person approves each entry

Clients are kept private; everything shown runs in production.

lumic gives each agent access to the screens and records its job needs, and nothing more. Every action it takes is logged.

# FAQ: FDEs, AI agents and approvals | lumic

> What an FDE is, where the agent runs, what it can touch, who approves its work, how long it takes to go live, and how lumic prices a job.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/faq/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

# Common questions about lumic.

What an FDE is, where the agent runs, what it can touch, who approves its work, how long it takes to go live, and how lumic prices a job.

Questions

## Plain answers.

### What is an FDE?

FDE stands for Forward Deployed Engineer. lumic’s FDEs are engineers who come to you, learn how the work is really done, build AI into one job at a time, and keep it working.

### Where does the agent run?

Wherever fits your business, on its own dedicated computer, under its own login, inside the systems you already run, whether that’s an ERP, accounting software, email, spreadsheets or cloud apps. To read a document, it uses a cloud AI model.

### What can the agent touch?

Only what its job needs. lumic gives each agent access to the screens and records its job needs, and nothing more. Every action it takes is logged.

### Who approves what the agent does?

A person on your team. The agent makes the entry, and a person checks it and approves it before anything posts. The final post stays in your hands.

### How long does it take to go live?

Weeks, not quarters. After the on-site day, lumic builds and tests the agent in your systems, then it goes live and lumic keeps it working.

### What does it cost?

It depends on the job. The consultation is free, and on-site work is $1,500/day, credited toward phase one. Managed AI from $250 to $5,000 a month, depending on scope. The build is a separate, one-time cost, priced in the written proposal. These figures are starting points, not quotes. Details: [Pricing](https://get-lumic.com/pricing/).

### Do you work outside St. Louis?

Yes. St. Louis first: the team is based here and comes on site in person. lumic travels for the right fit.

### Does lumic sell software?

No. lumic does not sell software to configure yourself; the team stays to run what it builds.

### What happens after an agent goes live?

lumic runs it for a monthly fee. The team watches it, tests it every month, fixes what breaks, and upgrades it as AI improves. A person on your team approves anything before it posts.

### What systems does lumic work with?

If your team runs it, lumic can work with it, whether that’s an ERP, accounting software, email, spreadsheets or cloud apps. The home page [lists the systems](https://get-lumic.com/#systems).

### Is lumic the right fit?

lumic fits a business with people doing repetitive work by hand, that wants it done inside the systems the team already uses, with a person approving what matters. lumic may not be the right fit for buyers who want a self-serve software license to set up themselves, or an agent that acts with no person approving.

- Cloud edition
- A person approves each entry

- Desktop edition
- Its own computer and login

### Alongside QuickBooks

Bills arrive by email, purchase orders may live in another system, and reports end up in spreadsheets. The agent works across the tools around your books, not just inside them.

- Email, spreadsheets, other systems
- One job, end to end

## Vendor bills in QuickBooks Desktop

The agent reads each vendor bill, matches it to the purchase order, and enters the bill in QuickBooks Desktop once a person approves it. When the purchase orders live in another system, it enters the bill there too, so nobody types it twice.

### It reads each bill.

The agent reads each vendor bill as it arrives by email, the same bill a clerk would open.

### It matches the PO.

It matches the bill to the purchase order and flags a price difference before anyone pays.

### A person approves, then it enters.

After a person approves it, the agent enters the bill in QuickBooks Desktop, and in the other system that holds the purchase orders, when there is one.

# Sage 100 AP automation, with a person posting every batch.

An agent reads each vendor bill, matches it to the purchase order, and prepares the AP invoice and the PO receipt in Sage 100, in an unposted batch. A person on your team reviews the batch and posts it. lumic builds it on site and keeps it working.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) See the job

## From the inbox to an unposted batch. A person posts it.

### A bill arrives by email.

The agent reads each vendor bill as it arrives by email, the same bill a clerk would open.

### It matches the PO.

It matches the bill to the purchase order in Sage 100.

### It prepares the batch.

It prepares the AP invoice and the PO receipt in an unposted Sage 100 batch, ready for a person to review.

## Flags before anyone pays.

When a bill does not match, the agent flags it for a person before it goes into the batch.

### Price off the PO

The bill’s price is not the price on the purchase order. The agent flags the difference for a person to approve.

- Flagged before anyone pays

### Quantity off the PO

The bill charges for more or less than the purchase order. The agent flags it for a person to check.

- Flagged before anyone pays

### A duplicate invoice number

The vendor’s invoice number is already in Sage 100. The agent flags it, so the same bill is not paid twice.

- Flagged before anyone pays

## Its own computer, its own login.

### Its own computer and login.

The agent works on its own dedicated computer, under its own login, inside the Sage 100 your team already uses.

### Access scoped to AP.

lumic gives the agent access to the AP screens and records its job needs, and nothing more.

### Every action logged.

Every action the agent takes is logged.

The post stays with you.

### A person posts every batch.

The agent prepares the batch and leaves it unposted. A person on your team reviews it and posts it. The final post stays in your hands.

### Gated by the people who know the work.

The agent leaves the batch unposted. Flagged bills wait for a person’s approval.

## Sage 100 AP automation, in plain answers.

### Can AI work with Sage 100?

Yes. A lumic agent works with Sage 100 on its own dedicated computer, under its own login. It reads each vendor bill, matches it to the PO, and prepares the AP invoice and PO receipt in an unposted batch. A person reviews the batch and posts it.

# Month-End Red Flags Service Firms Usually Miss | lumic

> Ten month-end mistakes in AP, billing, payroll and the close, on one page: a free checklist from lumic, with a PDF download.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/resources/month-end-red-flags/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

# Month-End Red Flags Service Firms Usually Miss

A short checklist for engineering firms, staffing firms, construction services and agencies. Each item is a habit that quietly slows the close or leaks margin. Count how many sound familiar.

[Download the PDF](https://get-lumic.com/resources/month-end-red-flags.pdf)

## Ten red flags.

### Unbilled time sitting past month-end.

Hours logged but not invoiced by the last day mean revenue lands a month late and cash follows even later.

### Vendor bills keyed twice, or not at all.

Bills arriving by email, portal and paper get entered by hand. Duplicates slip through, and missing ones show up as surprises after the close.

### Subcontractor and pass-through costs not matched to the job.

Costs that never get tagged to a project or client make job margin look better (or worse) than it is.

### Payroll journal entries built from a spreadsheet.

Copying payroll reports into an entry by hand invites misallocated wages, burden and accruals, especially across departments or jobs.

### Accrued payroll ignored at cutoff.

When a pay period crosses month-end and wages are not accrued, labor cost swings from month to month for no real reason.

### Cash receipts posted in a lump.

Deposits applied "on account" instead of to specific invoices leave aging reports wrong and collections chasing clients who already paid.

### Collections that start at 60 days.

Without a steady, polite reminder at the first missed due date, receivables age quietly while the team is busy delivering work.

### Recurring entries rebuilt every month.

Prepaids, depreciation, rent and software accruals typed fresh each close are slow and easy to get wrong.

### Tie-outs skipped when the close runs late.

Bank, AP, AR and payroll clearing accounts not reconciled before reports go out means leadership decides on numbers that will change.

### Reports exported and rebuilt by hand.

If revenue, margin and receivables come from a weekly export, the numbers are already stale when someone reads them.

Every one of these is a job an agent can take on. lumic builds AI agents that prepare bills, receipts, payroll entries and month-end entries in the systems a firm already runs, and a person approves each entry before anything posts.

Book a 20-minute call: [cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) · [hello@get-lumic.com](mailto:hello@get-lumic.com) · [get-lumic.com](https://get-lumic.com/)

# How to implement AI in a small business | lumic

> A practical method for putting AI to work in a small business: pick one job, map it, build inside your systems, keep a person on approval, and keep it working.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/resources/how-to-implement-ai-in-a-small-business/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

# How to implement AI in a small business, one job at a time.

Most small businesses do not need an AI strategy deck. They need one job done well by AI, inside the systems they already run, with a person approving what matters. This is the method lumic’s Forward Deployed Engineers use.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) The method

## Six steps, in order.

### Pick one job.

Start with the job that takes the most hours by hand and repeats every day or every month: entering bills, applying cash, keying orders, building the same entries or reports. One job, not a department.

### Watch it done by hand.

Sit beside the person who does it today. Write down the screens, the checks and the exceptions. The exceptions are where an AI project succeeds or fails.

### Remove steps before you automate them.

Some steps exist only because of an old workaround. Drop them. Then decide what needs AI, such as reading a document, and what only needs a plain rule.

### Build inside the systems you already run.

The agent should read and enter the same records a person would, whether that’s an ERP, accounting software, email, spreadsheets or cloud apps. No new system for the team to learn.

### Keep a person on approval.

The agent prepares each entry; a person checks it and approves it before anything posts. Give the agent access only to what its job needs, and log every action it takes. Test it on real work before it goes live.

### Keep it working.

Systems change, document layouts change, and AI models improve. Someone has to watch the agent, test it every month, fix what breaks and upgrade it. Then pick the following job.

[See the method on one agent, step by step: AP automation](https://get-lumic.com/services/ap-automation/)

## Four steps, from a free call to managed AI.

### Free consultation.

A 20‑minute call. You walk the team through the work your people do by hand.

- [Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call)

### On-site day and written proposal.

lumic’s FDEs work beside your team where the work happens and write a proposal. They map where AI fits; the proposal says what to build, the timeline, and the cost.

On-site work $1,500/day, credited toward phase one.

- [AI consulting](https://get-lumic.com/ai-consulting/)

### Build.

The team builds the agents, automations and dashboards inside your systems and sets up the approval step. Your team tests them on real work before they go live. lumic runs the job for you on a dedicated computer, or packages it for the AI assistant your team already uses.

Priced in the written proposal.

- [AI implementation](https://get-lumic.com/ai-implementation/)

### Managed AI.

lumic watches it, tests it every month, fixes what breaks, and upgrades it as AI improves. A person on your team approves what matters.

Managed AI from $250 to $5,000 a month, depending on scope.

- [Managed AI](https://get-lumic.com/managed-ai/)

# AI agents for accounting: what they do, how to start | lumic

> What an AI agent for accounting does: vendor bills, cash receipts, payroll entries and month-end, prepared in your systems for a person to approve.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/resources/ai-agent-for-accounting/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

# AI agents for accounting: what they do, and how to start.

An AI agent for accounting does one job a clerk does today, such as entering vendor bills or preparing month-end entries, inside the accounting software or ERP you already run. It prepares the entry; a person approves it before anything posts.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) The jobs that fit

## Repetitive, rule-bound, and checked by a person.

The best accounting jobs for an agent repeat every day or every month, follow rules a controller can write down, and already end in a review.

### Vendor bills

Read each bill from email, match it to the purchase order, flag a price difference, and enter it for approval.

[AP automation](https://get-lumic.com/services/ap-automation/)

### Cash receipts

Read remittances and payment detail, apply cash to open invoices, and leave each entry for a person to approve.

[Cash receipts and collections](https://get-lumic.com/services/cash-receipts-and-collections/)

### Payroll entries

Build the payroll journal entry from the payroll reports and check every line. The controller posts it.

[Payroll](https://get-lumic.com/services/payroll/)

### Month-end entries

Prepare the recurring entries and run the tie-outs. Every entry waits unposted until the controller posts it.

[Month-end close](https://get-lumic.com/services/month-end-close/)

### Reporting

Live dashboards read from the books, so nobody rebuilds the same report every morning. Dashboards only read.

[Dashboards and reporting](https://get-lumic.com/services/dashboards-and-reporting/)

## Gated by the people who know the work.

### A person approves every entry.

The agent prepares each entry. A person on your team checks it and approves it before anything posts, and the final post stays in your hands.

### Access is limited to the job.

Each agent works under its own login, with access to the screens and records its job needs, and nothing more.

### Everything is logged.

Every action an agent takes is logged, so a reviewer can see what it did and who approved it.

### Paused or revoked any time.

Any agent can be paused, or its access revoked, at any time.

## Start with the job that takes the most hours.

List the accounting jobs your team does by hand, with the hours each one takes. Pick one. Watch it done, write down the checks and the exceptions, then build the agent around how the work is really done.

### Free consultation.

On-site work $1,500/day, credited toward phase one.

Monthly pricing covers running and supporting your agents. The build is a separate, one-time cost, priced in the written proposal.

Final pricing depends on your workflow and systems. These figures are starting points, not quotes.
